The bottom panel of Figure 53 shows the sulfur TES cost, including the cost of external valves, fittings, piping and labor required for integrating sulfur TES with the solar field (denoted as 𝐶 in Eq. 23b). Focusing on a storage capacity 𝑇𝐸𝑆−𝑆𝐹−𝑖𝑛𝑡𝑒𝑔𝑟𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 of 550 MWh, it is observed that the LCOH initially decreases as the internal TES-HX specific surface area (A’) is reduced from 6 m2/m3 to 2.5 m2/m3. This reduction is attributed to the decrease in sulfur TES cost as illustrated in the bottom panel of Figure 53. Although further decrease in specific surface area reduces sulfur TES cost per unit energy capacity, the wider spacing of internal TES-HX tubes within sulfur TES reduces the charge/discharge heat transfer rates, thereby limiting system responsiveness. As a result, the LCOH increases for A’ < 2.5 m2/m3, indicating an optimal trade-off point. The lowest LCOH of 3.2 cents/kWh is obtained for a 720 MWh sulfur TES unit with an internal TES- HX specific surface area of 2.5 m2/m3. The corresponding sulfur TES cost per unit stored capacity is 33.6 $/kWh that satisfies the EOP-E target of 𝐶 < 45 $/kWh.
